newsitem.title: CANADA: Markborough sells property for US$35.6 mln.
newsitem.headline: Markborough sells property for US$35.6 mln.

text.p: Markborough Properties Inc on Tuesday said it completed the sale of its Washington, D.C. office building for US$35.6 million.

The real estate company said it sold the 155,000 square foot office building to Rosecliff Realty as part of a program announced in January to reduce debt by selling non-core assets. Markborough said it has now raised more than C$300 million (US$221.6 million) from divestitures since January.

The Toronto-based company also announced it increased its ownership in two shopping centers. Markborough said it closed its purchase of a 50 percent interest in Southcentre Mall in Calgary. The stake was held by the now-bankrupt Bramalea. Markborough said it also purchased an 8.3 percent interest in Les Galeries de la Capitale mall in Quebec City, boosting its stake to 33.3 percent.

The value of the transactions was about C$90 million, said Kim McInnes, president, land and office management with Markborough. McInnes said Markborough paid about C$22 million and assumed about C$68 million in debt to increase its stake in the two malls.
Markborough also outlined its progress in converting undeveloped land holdings to cash.
Markborough shares fell C$0.015 to C$0.385 in early afternoon trading. Some 44,000 shares changed had hands.
